chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Hampton's dishonesty, the mileage claim and show music
summary: Jack Kelso collected mileage through the union; Mingus calls Hampton crooked and soulless.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: dishonest people in the profession. They had guys out there, they'd tell them -- I wasn't the only one -- the guitar player that died not long ago, the -- one of the brothers?

Montgomery, yeah. They did the same thing to him. Ridiculous people, man. Get you out on the road and lower your salary. You can't get home, you're out somewhere on a bus, you don't know where you are. One guy, a guy named Jack Kelson, he took -- wrote down everything, every job they made and the amount of miles they travelled. And theatres, everything. And he took the money they gave him, but he went to the union and when (inaudible) he quit. And he got thousands and thousands of dollars just for the mileage. Big jumps, sometimes they'd do 2,000 miles on a bus. They had to pay him mileage and everything. You heard of that, mileage?
Yeah, I've heard of mileage, but not--
He got mileage. Everything, overtime -- the scale was higher than what I was asking for.

I had to get that down because [He just pulled a thing, he gave his word to] Lionel is still crooked. He was worried we'd go to a concert in South America for my manager. I never thought a person could be dishonest and play good, because all the guys that I know can play good are very honest, like Charlie Parker. Honest with themselves, honest with you. HE might take your money,
he might spend your money up, he might overdraw the salary and not pay you, but he'd tell you he did it.
He ain't going to pull no tricks on you.
(Inaudible) that's why Lionel don't have no soul. Never had any feeling in his playing.
Yeah. A lot of excitement, but --
